reviews.title: Great case on a budget itx/sfx
reviews.comment: Awesome case for itx motherboard and sfx power supply. If you run m-atx it’s going to be an air cooled build as it would cover intake fans. It does not fit rad and fans on top so 240aio has to be side mounted or a 120aio exhaust. You can fit an atx power supply but then not much room for the cables. That being said itx/sfx build/side mount aio was a breeze, used the ssd tray to store the fan hub. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Thinnest gauges steel I've ever seen
reviews.comment: This is the best looking case for ITX with two fans bottom and top!  All the big name brands try to check too many boxes on paper such as 120/140mm fan support, radiator/fan mounting brackets, and they just end up looking a mess.  This case: 1. Doesn't have a huge gap to the right of an ITX motherboard 2. Only has mounting holes for 120mm fans resulting in a clean look 3. Has room for a 240mm radiator on the side, with push and pull fans! 4. No support in the corner blocking your view 5. Tempered glass is nicely tinted for black version 6. Fits full size ATX power supply 7. Doesn't waste space trying to fit a 360mm radiator This is kinda cheap though, so there are some downsides: 1. You can bend this steel with your hands 2. The ventilation has way too much material-to-hole ratio, blocking airflow.  This goes for both the steel and magnetic screen/filter. 3. The height should have been raised 30mm above the motherboard to allow a radiator to be mounted on the top.  There is only room for fans, and adding a 30mm radiator would cause a collision with your RAM and CPU cooler. 4. The black strips on the glass edge should be as thin as possible to allow you to see the sides of your fans.  Unless you have ugly fans? I ended up cutting out the steel where fans are placed, and 3D printing fan filters with a 0.2mm nozzle instead.  Much better airflow.
reviews.author: Amazing customer

reviews.title: Bit of a disappointment
reviews.comment: The case is a bit flimsy and on the cheaper side. Too small for a proper fit of a m-atx board and too large for an itx board. Cable management took a long time because the routing is strange. Nowhere convenient to anchor cables to the case. Ended up replacing the cheap fans that were included. Mine only came with a top dust screen despite there being the exact same size and shape cutout on the bottom. I contacted customer service and they claimed that its only supposed to have one dust screen, so you get to choose if you want dust to get sucked in through the bottom or you can have an unfinished look on the top. Your choice. They would not sell me a spare dust screen. I do like the shape of it and the location of the psu mounted along the side panel in the back is pretty cool, but they should've raised it a tiny bit for better access to cable management. Alternatively you can mount a sff psu and have more space. I'm sure you can make this case work, but I've gotten great cases for the same price and this is not it.
